name: tiff-visualizer
description: Rust-based decoding and GPU rendering for more than 25 integer and floating-point image formats, with precise pixel inspection, multidimensional navigation, interactive visualization, comparison, and layer compositing.

tiffVisualizer.navigationShortcuts.markdownDescription: Override shared image navigation keys by control position (1–4). Each pair is [previous, next]. Use physical codes such as `KeyJ`, `KeyK`, `BracketLeft`, or `Shift+Comma`; a single character such as `j` or `ü` follows the layout. Example: `{"1": ["KeyJ", "KeyK"]}`. Omitted/invalid pairs use defaults. A lone slice slider uses pair 2. Hints show the active bindings. Shortcuts apply while the preview has focus; avoid keys used by other viewer tools.

tiffVisualizer.channels.autoComposite.description: Open images whose channels are described by OME-TIFF or ImageJ metadata (fluorescence stacks, hyperstacks) in composite mode. Ordinary RGB images are not affected. Turning composite off by hand keeps it off for that preview.

tiffVisualizer.channels.autoOpenPanel.description: Open the Channels panel when an image whose channels are described by OME-TIFF or ImageJ metadata opens. For multi-page stacks it opens before the other channels have decoded, so the loading progress is visible. Applies once per file; ordinary RGB images are not affected.

tiffVisualizer.channels.colorsByName.description: Channel tints by channel name, matched case-insensitively, for example {"DAPI": "#3399ff", "GFP": "#00ff00"}. Takes precedence over colorsByNumber and over colours stored in the file.

tiffVisualizer.channels.colorsByNumber.description: Channel tints by channel number as shown in the Channels panel (starting at 1), for example {"1": "#00ff00"}. Takes precedence over colours stored in the file.

tiffVisualizer.channels.groups.description: Named groups of channels for the Channels panel, for example {"T Cells": ["CD3e", "CD8", "CD4"]}. Each value lists channel names (exact, case-insensitive) or 1-based channel numbers. A group can be switched on or off, or soloed, as a unit.

enumDescriptions: Open the Channels panel, which ends in the Cells section, for multichannel OME-TIFF images with a micron scale, which is what fluorescence microscopy looks like. Other images never see it.
Open the Channels panel with its Cells section for every image.
Never open it by itself. Right-click the image and choose Cells, or run Scientific Image Visualizer: Cells.
tiffVisualizer.cells.autoOpenPanel.description: When the Channels panel and its Cells section open by themselves. It opens once per file, so closing it is not undone as you step through Z or T.

path.description: Path of the table, for example segtraq/{sample_name}/{sample_name}.segtraq_cells.parquet.

parent.description: Name of the one cell set the table belongs to: Xenium cells, or a name from tiffVisualizer.cells.cellBoundariesParquet.

tiffVisualizer.cells.cellsParquet.description: Extra cell tables for Xenium bundles, as name → {path, parent}, for example {"xenium_segtraq": {"path": "segtraq/{sample_name}/{sample_name}.segtraq_cells.parquet", "parent": "Xenium cells"}}. Each file needs a cell_id column. It is listed under its parent cell set only, and its columns are merged into that set by cell_id when you click Load. The parent is Xenium cells (the bundle's own cells) or a name from tiffVisualizer.cells.cellBoundariesParquet. {sample_name} is the name of the folder that holds experiment.xenium. Relative paths start at the workspace folder.

tiffVisualizer.transcripts.groups.description: Gene groups for the Transcripts section of Xenium bundles, as name → gene list, for example {"Epithelial": ["EPCAM", "KRT8"]}, or name → {genes, color} to choose the group colour. Groups are offered in the Transcripts section's Add group list; none is added until you pick it. Groups can also be made in the panel, from a pasted list of gene names.

tiffVisualizer.cells.cellBoundariesParqu.description: Extra cell segmentations for Xenium bundles, as name → path, for example {"sam2": "sam2/{sample_name}/cell_boundaries.parquet"}. Each file is a Xenium-style cell_boundaries.parquet (cell_id, vertex_x, vertex_y in microns). {sample_name} is the name of the folder that holds experiment.xenium. Relative paths start at the workspace folder. Segmentations are listed in the Cells section and loaded when you click Load.

path.description: Path of the nucleus boundaries file, for example sam2/{sample_name}/nucleus_boundaries.parquet.

parent.description: Name of the one cell set the nuclei belong to: Xenium cells, or a name from tiffVisualizer.cells.cellBoundariesParquet.

tiffVisualizer.cells.nucleusBoundariesPa.description: Extra nucleus outlines for Xenium bundles, as name → {path, parent}, for example {"sam2_nuclei": {"path": "sam2/{sample_name}/nucleus_boundaries.parquet", "parent": "sam2"}}. Each file is a Xenium-style nucleus_boundaries.parquet (cell_id, vertex_x, vertex_y in microns) whose cell ids match its parent. It is listed under its parent cell set only and loaded when you click Load; a cell set shows one nucleus file at a time, so loading one replaces the previous. {sample_name} is the name of the folder that holds experiment.xenium. Relative paths start at the workspace folder.

tiffVisualizer.gpuAcceleration.description: Use GPU acceleration via WebGPU or WebGL2 for supported image rendering paths. Disable this if a GPU/driver causes incorrect output or slower rendering.

tiffVisualizer.experimentalRegionDecode.description: Experimental: use rectangle reads for images that have NO resolution pyramid, so the cost of a view follows the window rather than the file. Pyramidal images (Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, whole-slide) do this already whenever their level is set to Auto, and are unaffected by this setting. Nothing uses it yet for images without a pyramid: drawing those a region at a time needs the canvas to become a window onto the image, which is not implemented.

scripts.build:wasm: cd wasm/tiff-decoder && RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=+simd128" wasm-pack build --target web --release && cd ../.. && mkdir -p media/wasm && cp wasm/tiff-decoder/pkg/tiff_wasm.js media/wasm/tiff-wasm.js && cp wasm/tiff-decoder/pkg/tiff_wasm_bg.wasm media/wasm/tiff-wasm.wasm && node -e "const fs=require('fs');const f='media/wasm/tiff-wasm.js';fs.writeFileSync(f,fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8').replace(/tiff_wasm_bg\.wasm/g,'wasm/tiff-wasm.wasm'))" && node scripts/strip-wasm-names.mjs media/wasm/tiff-wasm.wasm
scripts.build:wasm:codecs: cd wasm/tiff-decoder && RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=+simd128" wasm-pack build --target web --release --out-dir pkg-codecs --out-name codec_wasm --features heavy-codecs && cd ../.. && mkdir -p media/wasm && cp wasm/tiff-decoder/pkg-codecs/codec_wasm.js media/wasm/codec-wasm.js && cp wasm/tiff-decoder/pkg-codecs/codec_wasm_bg.wasm media/wasm/codec-wasm.wasm && node -e "const fs=require('fs');const f='media/wasm/codec-wasm.js';fs.writeFileSync(f,fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8').replace(/codec_wasm_bg\.wasm/g,'wasm/codec-wasm.wasm'))" && node scripts/strip-wasm-names.mjs media/wasm/codec-wasm.wasm
scripts.build:wasm:jxl: cd wasm/jxl-decoder && RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=+simd128" wasm-pack build --target web --release && cd ../.. && mkdir -p media/wasm && cp wasm/jxl-decoder/pkg/jxl_wasm.js media/wasm/jxl-wasm.js && cp wasm/jxl-decoder/pkg/jxl_wasm_bg.wasm media/wasm/jxl-wasm.wasm && node -e "const fs=require('fs');const f='media/wasm/jxl-wasm.js';fs.writeFileSync(f,fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8').replace(/jxl_wasm_bg\.wasm/g,'wasm/jxl-wasm.wasm'))" && node scripts/strip-wasm-names.mjs media/wasm/jxl-wasm.wasm
scripts.build:wasm:transcripts: RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=+simd128" CC_wasm32_unknown_unknown="${CC_wasm32_unknown_unknown:-$PWD/scripts/zig-cc-wasm32.sh}" AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown="${AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown:-ar}" cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p transcripts-wasm --no-default-features --features c-zstd && mkdir -p media/wasm && cp target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/transcripts_wasm.wasm media/wasm/transcripts-wasm.wasm && node scripts/strip-wasm-names.mjs media/wasm/transcripts-wasm.wasm
